findings.title: Relocating out of an unverified synced folder leaves the id in `unverified`, so moves stay refused
findings.body: `availabilityOf` adds an id to `unverified` when a synced folder's probe times out (line 191). It removes it only when a synced probe answers (line 182). Line 179 returns early for a non-synced workspace without clearing it. After `relocateFolder` points such a workspace at a plain folder, `syncStates.refresh` makes `of()` return null. `availabilityOf` then takes the early return at line 179, and the stale id stays in the set. `resolveMoveSide` (line 206) returns null for it, so every move from or to that workspace is refused as "not connected" until a restart or until it is synced again. Nothing tells the user why. Fix: call `unverified.delete(id)` on the early-return path at line 179, or in `relocateFolder` after the refresh. I did not read the move caller that turns the null into the refusal reason.

contracts.action: Relocate a workspace: re-detect the sync provider of the new folder, probe availability (bounded if synced), and return the updated workspace view
contracts.equivalent_path: addWorkspace (lines 577-612) and createWorkspace (lines 628-647) call syncStates.refresh, then availabilityOf, then toWorkspaceView with syncStates.of(entry)
contracts.before_after: The siblings refresh sync state before availabilityOf, and the new code does the same. It also re-reads the entry from the registry, because relocation may have changed the path. Before this change relocate returned no workspace view.
contracts.visible_effect: The renderer gets the workspace view with the new availability and sync provider. broadcastState also pushes the state to the windows.
contracts.failure_mode: The `unverified` set is not cleared when a workspace moves from a synced folder to a plain one (see finding). `detectSync` is bounded by a timeout in synced-folder.ts. I did not verify that it never rejects, so a rejection would fail the IPC call after the relocation has already been committed.
contracts.open_question: Does detectSync ever reject, and what do callers do with the null that resolveMoveSide returns?
